title: auth-api-401-429-debug-scratchpad
content:
Context / summary:
- Intermittent 401 and 429 errors observed for customer requests over last 48h. Patterns look like: most requests succeed, but a small fraction (0.5-2%) either 401 or 429. Reports come from multiple regions (us-west1, eu-west1).
- Appears correlated with bursts of traffic from a handful of API keys + some internal traffic spikes.
- Ticket SUP-2943 opened by CS with sample request_ids and timestamps.

Observed error examples (raw snippets):
- 401 responses:
  HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
  Content-Type: application/json
  X-Request-ID: r-0a1b2c3d
  {"error":"Invalid API key", "code":401, "request_id":"r-0a1b2c3d"}

  Another sample (same key, 2s later):
  HTTP/1.1 200 OK
  {"id":"resp-....", "choices": [...] }

- 429 responses:
  HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
  Content-Type: application/json
  Retry-After: 1
  X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
  X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
  {"error":"Quota exceeded: per-minute rate limit exceeded", "code":429, "request_id":"r-9f8e7d6c"}

Hypotheses / notes:
1) API key rotation / partial revocation: improbable because same key works for many requests, and there were no recent rotation events in the key audit log for that customer. Need to re-check KMS logs.
2) Rate limiter enforcement race: a race between distributed rate-limit counters could produce transient 401 if auth service mistakenly classifies as expired/invalid while ratelimit path returns 429 for other nodes. Unclear why 401 would be emitted by rate limiter though.
3) Token cache invalidation bug in edge nodes: if cached token metadata expires earlier than central store, node could reject with 401, then refresh and succeed.
4) Quota/account-level throttling: per-customer quotas enforced at a different layer than per-key; misalignment can cause 429 from quota layer and 401 from auth layer (if account set to restricted state).
5) Clock skew between nodes causing temporary signature validation failures = 401. Need to inspect NTP drift on nodes that served 401s.

Commands / stuff I ran (repro attempts):
- curl (replay):
  export API_KEY="sk_live_customer123"
  curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"gpt-test","input":"hello"}' \
    https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate > /tmp/replay.out 2>&1
  # saw interleaved 200/401/429 across repeated runs (in same 30s window)

- python minimal loop to hit same key and print status + headers:
  ```python
  import requests, time
  API_KEY = "sk_live_customer123"
  for i in range(200):
      r = requests.post("https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate",
                        headers={"Authorization":f"Bearer {API_KEY}", "Content-Type":"application/json"},
                        json={"model":"gpt-test","input":"hi"})
      print(i, r.status_code, r.headers.get('X-Request-ID'), r.headers.get('X-RateLimit-Remaining'))
      time.sleep(0.1)
  ```
  # Observed pattern: sometimes status_code==401 with X-Request-ID present, X-RateLimit-Remaining varies.

- tcpdump on bastion + nginx access logs filtered by request_id: collected for a few windows. Saved pcap to /tmp/auth-replay-2026-03-30.pcap.

Logs / interesting lines: (redacted customer/key ids)
- auth-service (auth-2) 2026-03-30T14:12:05Z - WARN - token validation failed for key sk_live_customer123 - reason: signature_mismatch - node_id=node-12
- auth-service (auth-7) 2026-03-30T14:12:05Z - INFO - token validation succeeded for key sk_live_customer123 - node_id=node-87
- rate-limiter (rl-5) 2026-03-30T14:12:06Z - ERROR - quota exceeded for customer cust-456 - window=60s - count=121 limit=120

Correlations noticed:
- 401s cluster around node-12 (see logs above). Node-12 shows more NTP sync warnings in last week.
- 429s correspond to rl-5 which is in same AZ as node-12. Possible partial outage/partition causing retry storms hitting same limiter.

What I checked and ruled out quickly:
- Key revoked? No (checked key management audit).
- Billing/quota changes? Customer quota unchanged last 30d.
- Recent deploys? Canary deploy for auth-service on 2026-03-29 02:00 UTC touched nodes node-11..node-15. PR #1187. Might be related.
- WAF / CDN blocking? No matching rules.

Immediate next steps (short):
- Reproduce in staging with controlled burst to verify race/HTTP code mix. Create identical canary nodes with NTP skew and see behavior. (OWNER: me)
- Increase auth-service debug logging and capture full validation error details for node-12 during next window. (OWNER: Samir)
- Temporarily add extra monitoring for X-RateLimit-Remaining and custom metric when 401 emitted within 5s of 200 for same key. (OWNER: Oliver)
- Rollback canary on auth-service nodes node-11..node-15 if we see clear repro. (OWNER: Release Eng)

Longer-term hypotheses to validate:
- Fix: ensure auth cache TTLs aligned and implement atomic refresh to avoid "transient invalid" states.
- Fix: unify quota and auth error mapping so that only 429 produced for quota, 401 only for genuine auth failures.
- Fix: harden NTP monitoring / alerting and roll out time-sanity checks at process start.

Notes to CS / Support replies (draft):
- "We’re actively investigating intermittent 401/429 errors for a small subset of requests. We’ve identified a potential correlation with a recent canary deploy of the auth service and are collecting additional logs. Could you please provide any sample request IDs you’ve seen and the timestamps? That will help us map to our internal traces. Also, please confirm if customer is seeing increased burst traffic patterns or scheduled jobs around the times of failures."

Random ideas to try quickly:
- Add short jittered backoff client-side for 429s; for 401s, capture raw response headers and request ids and retry once after 100-300ms to see if it’s transient.
- Instrument the edge to log local time vs NTP time at request start to detect skew on live traffic.

Files / artifacts saved locally:
- /tmp/replay.out (curl verbose outputs)
- /tmp/auth-replay-2026-03-30.pcap (tcpdump)
- logs pulled into s3://redwood-debug/auth-401-429/2026-03-30/ (see linked_artifacts Slack thread for presigned links)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is node-12 acting as leader for some quota windows? Why does one node show signature_mismatch while another simultaneously validates.
- Does rate-limiter cache partition cause different views of remaining tokens?
- Confirm whether any infra change touched chrony/ntp config in last 7 days.

If I don't get to this tomorrow: escalate to infra-ops with pcap + one sample 401 request_id + node-12 logs and ask for NTP check on node-12.

-- Lena
